issues.title: Replaced 9-5 turbo can be damaged by dry start or faulty oil/coolant connections
issues.cause: Factory installation procedure requires oil in floating bearing housing before startup and renewed oil/coolant copper seals; service disassembly can damage exhaust bellows or charge-air hose sealing.
symptoms: recent turbo replacement with immediate whine/smoke
issues.diagnosis_summary: Before condemning replacement turbo, inspect documented priming, correct oil-feed supply/return, leaks, coolant routing, and hose clamps. Do not run a knowingly oil-starved or overheated engine.
issues.correction_summary: Repair verified oil/coolant/hose sealing or installation errors with correct factory procedure. Escalate to turbo replacement only after measurable mechanical damage.
limits: Oil priming does not guarantee an undamaged used turbo or healthy engine bearings.
MY2008 shaft-play numerical limit not recovered.
Do not apply torque values to oil cooler/gearbox banjos.

issues.title: 9-5 FA57 electrical solenoid class differentiation before declaring valve body/gearbox failure
issues.cause: S1–S5 de-energized shift valves are distinct from PWM pressure control SLT/SLS and torque converter lock-up SLU, with substantially different winding resistance.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Read TCM DTC, actual temperature and solenoid assignment, verify matched physical gearbox/TCM, perform qualified resistance and wiring tests before considering internal hydraulic damage.
issues.correction_summary: Repair a proven electrical/signal or valve-body fault where feasible; do not automatically rebuild the transmission or assume new solenoid cures worn clutches.
limits: Coil resistance in normal range does not establish mechanical hydraulic function.
5.1–5.5 descriptive range versus 5.0–5.6 technical table not evidence of redesign.
No verified OE replacement solenoid number or 2026 VIN fitment.

issues.title: Similar 440-2181/440-2182 bulletins must not contaminate MY2005–09 9-5 automatic diagnosis
issues.cause: 440-2181 concerns OG9-3 and 440-2182 OG9-5 MY1998–99 with Dexron III ATF; later OG9-5 FA57 Saab 3309 is a different original service specification.
symptoms: online search suggests Dexron III from an older common-faults bulletin
2008 9-5 claimed to need 1998 ground strap G41S
issues.diagnosis_summary: Read original car/platform/year/market and bulletin number, separately identify gearbox and current original WIS ATF grade. Do not generalize early four-speed fault remedies to later FA57.
issues.correction_summary: Use 2005–09 FA57 source-specific Saab 3309 documentation and matching TCM/gearbox diagnosis; preserve early bulletins only for their actual populations.
limits: Neither bulletin authorizes Dexron III in MY2005–09 FA57.
Ground points G41S/G41P/G43 are MY1998–99 bulletin only.
Factory bulletins are symptom-specific and not universal 9-5 failure statistics.
